transcript.text: SFC Patel, that's an important catch. Let me address it directly. The 12-hour rest rule as stated in our company policy applies between assigned shifts — 'between the end of one assigned shift and the start of its next assigned shift.' The medical screening is a personnel-readiness restriction, not an assigned shift on the support-team roster. So the 12-hour rest rule does not apply between the medical screening and the Thursday day shift. Bravo's medical screening ends at 1900 Wednesday, and Bravo's Thursday day shift starts at 0600. That's 11 hours, but since the screening is not an assigned shift, the rest rule is not triggered. Bravo is available for Thursday day shift as directed by higher headquarters. That resolves the conflict you flagged. Now, let me summarize where we stand. We have three update commitments: Lt. Brooks for the operations calendar update on Bravo's Thursday day shift evaluation tasking, SFC Alvarez for the motor-pool update on Alpha's heavy-vehicle qualification, and SFC Patel for the personnel system update on Bravo's medical screening restriction and Delta's replacement designation. The proposed roster is: Delta on Wednesday day, Alpha on Wednesday night, and Bravo on Thursday day. All three teams get at least 12 hours rest between assigned shifts — Delta finishes at 1800 Wednesday and is not assigned again, Alpha finishes at 0600 Thursday and is not assigned again, and Bravo has no prior assigned shift before Thursday day. If there are no further flags from the scrub, I'm prepared to settle on this roster and sign once all three update commitments are confirmed. Are there any other discrepancies anyone needs to flag before I finalize?
